title: Release velocity, acceptance canvas, and ops task tracker
content:
Purpose: One-page, operationally focused tracker that blends a lightweight velocity heatmap, acceptance criteria canvas, and an execution task checklist for small-to-medium releases. Intended for product ops to drive go/no-go decisions, highlight capacity bottlenecks, and surface post-release remediation tasks.

Context and use:
- This doc is used during the last 3 sprints of a release cycle.
- Owners update the velocity heatmap weekly and mark acceptance gates as pass/warn/fail.
- Product, engineering, QA, SRE, and PS (solutions engineering) should all sign off on their gates prior to canary.

1) High-level release summary
- Release name: R-Velocity Q4 adaptive-batching
- Release window: 2025-11-03 -> 2025-11-17 (canary 2 days -> ramp)
- Release lead: Maya Patel (product-ops)
- Primary stakeholders: Eng-serving-runtime, Eng-observability, Sales-PLG

2) Velocity heatmap (weekly snapshots; color-coded guidance below)
- How to read: rows = teams/subsystems, cols = weeks; cells = % of planned work closed (velocity). Add notes for blocked issues.
- Current snapshot (week labels abbreviated):
  Week -2: backlog grooming and infra prep
  Week -1: feature freeze, integration tests
  Week 0: canary start

  Rows:
  - Serving-runtime: 85% | 92% | 70% (note: performance regression in long-seq tests)
  - Console+Rollouts: 60% | 78% | 95% (rollback UX updated)
  - Observability: 40% | 55% | 65% (agent upgrade delayed)
  - SRE: 90% | 88% | 80% (capacity tuning pending)

- Color guidance: >=90% green, 70–89% amber (monitor closely), <70% red (blocking).

3) Acceptance canvas (gating criteria per area)
- Criterion format: Owner | Gate | Measure | Threshold | Current state | Notes

  a) Model-serving correctness | Eng-serving-runtime | Integration test suite pass rate | >=99% | amber (97.3%) | Failing on cross-batch KV cache edge-case.
  b) Latency SLOs | SRE | P95 gen latency (canary traffic) | <=220ms | green | Canary measured 185ms for short seq.
  c) Cost regression | Finance/Product | Per-token cost delta | <= +12% | green | Quantization savings offset some spikes.
  d) Console release controls | Console team | Rollout toggles working in staging | pass/fail | green | Canary toggle validated.
  e) Observability completeness | Observability | Tracing + error-rate dashboards present | pass/fail | amber | Missing a tracer tag for model variant.
  f) Security & policy | Security+Compliance | No open high-risk findings | pass/fail | green | Awaiting final audit note (low severity).

- Gate decision rules: 0 red gates -> proceed; 1+ amber -> require mitigation plan and partial hold; 1+ red -> block release. Record overrides with exec approver and rationale.

4) Go/no-go scoreboard (one-line per stakeholder)
- Product: Maya Patel -> PROVISIONAL (monitoring mitigation).
- Eng-serving-runtime: Elliot Chu -> PROVISIONAL (fix in flight, ETA 48h).
- SRE: Priya Singh -> YES (capacity health ok).
- Security: Rafael Gomez -> YES (low severity only).

5) Pre-canary ops checklist (must be ticked before canary traffic)
- [ ] Canary environment snapshot taken and pinned (owner: SRE)
- [ ] Traffic routing policy prepared and rollback target defined (owner: Console)
- [ ] Observability dashboards added to release folder (owner: Observability)
- [ ] Smoke test script verified with synthetic queries (owner: QA)
- [ ] Secret rotation and KMS config validated for private deployments (owner: Security)
- [ ] Cost monitoring alert thresholds set (owner: Finance/Product)
- [ ] Post-deploy runbook stub created (owner: Product-ops)

6) Canary gating runbook (lightweight)
- Step 0: Start canary at 5% of user traffic for 2 hours. Monitor P95 latency, error rate, and smoke-test success.
- Step 1: If all acceptance gates green -> increase to 25% for 4 hours.
- Step 2: If amber -> hold and trigger mitigation sprint lane (attach JIRA epic).
- Step 3: If red -> immediate rollback and postmortem assignment.

7) Risk matrix (top 6 risks and mitigations)
- Regression in long-seq performance -> mitigation: run extended perf suite nightly + pre-canary subset; owner Eng-serving-runtime.
- Observability gaps -> mitigation: ship tracer tag patch and validate dashboards; owner Observability.
- Infra capacity mis-estimate -> mitigation: SRE to enable short-term burst capacity; owner SRE.
- Cost spike due to burstiness -> mitigation: throttle policy + cost alerts; owner Finance/Product.
- Rollout toggle fails -> mitigation: manual rollback script + runbook; owner Console.
- Uncaptured customer integration -> mitigation: contact top 10 customers and schedule advisory deployment window; owner Solutions Eng.

8) Post-release acceptance and KPI tracker (30-day lookback)
- Primary KPIs to monitor (owner):
  - P95 latency (SRE) — baseline vs +1/4/30 days
  - Error rate (Observability) — anomaly detection alerts
  - Tokenized cost per 1M tokens (Finance) — track weekly
  - Feature adoption (Product) — % of traffic using new batching path
  - Rollback incidents (Product-ops) — target 0 major incidents

- Data cadence: daily for first 72h, weekly thereafter up to day 30.

9) Outstanding ops tasks (action tracker)
- ACTION-001: Fix KV cache edge case failing integration (assignee: Elliot Chu) — ETA 2025-11-05 — status: in_progress.
- ACTION-002: Add tracer tag to model variant and re-index dashboards (assignee: Rafael Gomez) — ETA 2025-11-04 — status: todo.
- ACTION-003: Update cost alert thresholds to include burst signal (assignee: Maya Patel & Finance) — ETA 2025-11-03 — status: in_review.
- ACTION-004: Draft postmortem template for canary rollback (assignee: Product-ops) — ETA 2025-11-06 — status: todo.

10) Stakeholder sign-off and escalation path
- Quick signoff checklist: each primary owner posts a short signoff message in #release-signoff Slack and links a documented artifact (dashboard, test run, ticket).
- Escalation path: Release lead -> Head of Product Ops -> VP Eng -> CTO. Any exec override must be recorded with timestamp and justification in this doc.

11) Notes, decisions, and open questions
- Decision: proceed with canary despite amber observability gate because mitigations (tracer tag patch) can be merged within 24h and canary scope limited to non-critical tenants.
- Open Q: Do we want to pre-notify customers who have private deployments about the canary window? (action: Solutions Eng to draft advisory email).

12) Quick links and artifacts
- Perf suite results: linked_artifacts[1]
- Canary dashboard (staging): dashboard url placeholder
- Runbook template: confluence runbook id

Change log (high-level):
- 2025-10-14: initial draft created by Maya Patel
- 2025-10-21: added velocity heatmap and initial gate states (Elliot Chu)
- 2025-11-02: updated canary schedule and action ETAs (Product-ops)

Usage guidance: keep this doc intentionally lightweight. For larger, multi-quarter launches use the more formal launch playbook. This canvas is for tactical release-level decisioning and rapid iteration on gating criteria and operational handoffs.

End of doc.
